sources.title: State Archive of Modena: Historical holdings and the Este state
sources.note: Direct/indexed official archive: Ferrara lost in 1598, capital transferred to Modena, Napoleonic administrations 1796 to 1814, Francesco V left June 1859.

sources.title: State Archive of Modena: A guide to the archive
sources.note: Indexed original Ministry archive guide, printed pages 44 to 45: 28 August 1814 plan of government, centralized ducal control; 1859 deposition and August assembly decrees, provisional governments.

sources.title: City of Modena: Waterways and everyday work
sources.note: Direct municipal exhibition text: 1684 Boccabadati map, mid-seventeenth-century Darsena, 1667 sloping loading system, washwomen, canals, water power, artesian wells and public fountains. Source covers multiple centuries; undated continuities are not assigned invented event years.

sources.title: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia: Institutional history
sources.note: Direct university history: renewed teaching 1682, statutes 1685, municipal/donated finance, eight chairs; direct ducal control and funding in 1772.

sources.title: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia: Bernardino Ramazzini
sources.note: Direct/indexed university commemoration: Carpi birth, Modena medical chair 1682 and 1700 publication; moved to Padua. Avoids first-ever absolute claims.

sources.title: University of Iowa: Ramazzini’s 1700 first edition
sources.note: Direct rare-book catalogue, Heirs of Hippocrates 592: De morbis artificum diatriba, Modena, Typis Antonii Capponi, 1700. Title transcribed from catalogue of actual first edition, not invented Latin. Catalogue occupation count conflicts with CNRS edition-specific account, so no number used.

sources.title: CNRS: Ramazzini and occupational health
sources.note: Direct research institution account. Uses translated expanded 1713 text, later reprinted; specific dust/laundry observations explicitly attributed to expanded treatise, not assumed all present in 1700 or all observed in Modena.

sources.title: City of Modena: Palazzo dei Musei and its earlier uses
sources.note: Direct/indexed official municipal history: poorhouse built 1764 to 1771, subsistence and work, transformation into Albergo delle Arti in 1788, later Napoleonic military use. Does not establish voluntary residence or modern welfare rights.

sources.title: AGO Modena cultural foundation: Building the hospital
sources.note: Indexed original foundation historical account; direct tool failed. First part inaugurated 30 November 1758, foundation medals commissioned from Pietro Sola. No bed count used.

sources.title: University Botanical Garden of Modena: History
sources.note: Direct/indexed university garden history: 1758 medicinal plant garden, 1765 public botany chair, 1772 university administration, central pool and medicinal beds.

sources.title: State Archive of Parma: General guide
sources.note: Direct official PDF. Printed 370 to 371 dynasties; printed 391 Napoleonic administration after 9 October 1802, conscription and civil code 1805, Taro department 24 May 1808; printed 410 to 411 provisional government 1859.

sources.title: Glauco Lombardi Museum: Parma in 1816
sources.note: Direct/indexed museum research publication: Magawly administration from July 1814 under Austrian direction; Maria Luigia arrived 20 April 1816 following Vienna settlement.

sources.title: Italian Ministry of Culture: Piacenza and the Risorgimento
sources.note: Direct official archival exhibition. Liberation and unity section: duchess departed 9 June 1859, Austrian troops left Piacenza 10 June, municipal union vote and provisional authorities.

sources.title: University of Parma: Institutional history
sources.note: Direct/indexed university history: 1768 educational constitutions from primary to university level; physics cabinets, anatomical theaters, veterinary teaching and learned institutions. No claim of achieved universal schooling.

sources.title: University of Parma: History of chemistry at San Rocco
sources.note: Indexed original university historical publication, printed page 5: first chemistry chair in medicine 1767; former Jesuit San Rocco premises became ducal university 1768 after expulsion. Uses institutional detail rather than unsupported laboratory safety claims.

sources.title: Palatina Library: Its founding and catalogues
sources.note: Direct institutional account: 1761 public-benefit foundation, Paciaudi collected books, movable catalogue slips included location and bibliographic evaluations; official opening May 1769.

sources.title: Bodoni Museum: Biography and historical editions
sources.note: Direct museum source. 1768 royal printing shop and housing in Pilotta; 1769 festival-book caption supplies exact Italian title sample. Caption is used as transcription, not image-view claim. Museum text contains unrelated obvious date typo in Rome section and broad 1802 annexation shorthand; neither repeated.

sources.title: Bodoni Museum: The 1818 typographic manual
sources.note: Direct museum source: Margherita Dall’Aglio continued printing shop and issued posthumous two-volume Manuale in 1818. More than 600 plates and over 1000 ornaments stated; totals not needed.

sources.title: Parmigiano Reggiano Museum: Seventeenth-century development
sources.note: Direct/indexed food museum account and transcription of 7 August 1612 notarial geographical-name document. Explicitly before map interval. Avoids equating early designation with modern legal PDO system.

sources.title: Emilia-Romagna cultural heritage catalogue: Casino Petitot
sources.note: Indexed original regional catalogue. Boulevard 720 m, coffee pavilion at eastern end, opening 24 June 1766 and traditional outdoor dew walk. Direct canonical printcard request failed. No first-ever café claim.

sources.title: City of Parma: The old hospital
sources.note: Direct official municipal visitor account: eighteenth-century split Misericordia and Esposti; about 300 patients in first section, foundling care in second. Public text uses purposes but not capacity to avoid conflating dates.

sources.title: Pilotta Museum: Celebrations in the Farnese Theatre
sources.note: Direct museum source: built 1618, opened 1628, used only nine times for costly dynastic celebrations, last occasion 1732.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported repeated polygon, 1650 to 1815, bbox 9.8263,43.8805 to 11.3383,45.0665, reaches too far north toward Mantua. Public overview warns against exact border reading and explains 1796 to 1814 interruption; no geometry changes. Narrative follows Duchy of Modena/Reggio, not city alone.

Imported repeated 1650 to 1815 polygon, bbox 9.1315,44.3568 to 10.3951,45.2199. Broad Parma/Piacenza corridor; no attempt to infer fixed borders through all phases. Public overview identifies French 1802/1808 change and post-1815 restoration continuity. Food rule explicitly 1612 background, widow printing explicitly 1818 later evidence.
